To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have fine mapped 9 positional candidate regions for ADHD in an extended ASP sample of 308 families and have found evidence of linkage on chromosomes 5p13 and 17p, as well as evidence of linkage and suggestive evidence of linkage on chromosome 6q12 and 16p13 respectively.
we have completed fine mapping of 9 positional candidate regions for ADHD in an extended population-based sample of 308 ASPs.

we have completed fine mapping of the four most promising chromosomal regions identified in three genomewide scans of ADHD and have confirmed linkage in each region, with the strongest evidence for linkage on 6p12 and 17p12 and suggestive evidence on 16p13 and 5p13.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying genes that confer susceptibility to ADHD.
identifying genetic risk factors for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (AD/HD), a common neurobehavioral disorder that is characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity.
identifying the genetic basis of ADHD, a disorder of childhood that has significant impact on the individual's life course and on society at large.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence of linkage to ADHD on 6q, 16p and 17p is now strong.
the linkage results for ADHD have been strengthened by this report.
the linkage findings for ADHD are consistent and compelling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study support the existence of at least four susceptibility genes for ADHD and suggest that the heritable component of ADHD is not due to a single gene.
we have identified four regions on chromosomes 5, 6, 16, and 17 that are likely to harbor susceptibility loci for ADHD.
we have found four regions that are likely to harbor susceptibility loci for ADHD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
linkage analyses in large samples are still an effective strategy for the identification of ADHD susceptibility genes.
the linkage results are robust and reproducible, and that the linkage results can be used as a basis for subsequent genetic studies of ADHD.
genomewide linkage analysis of ADHD in large samples of affected sib pairs can be successfully used to fine map the chromosomal locations of ADHD susceptibility genes.
